summary: Ryoshin Nakao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1971 to 1979, and later held posts at the Research Institute of Soto Studies and Hanazono University around 1995.

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, teaching at Taisho University where he served as professor from 1975, dean in 1981, and professor emeritus from 1990 to 1994.

Ryosho Nakamura (1927–2013) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University, later serving as professor at The International University of Kagoshima from around 1960 to 1998.
Ryosho Onami is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Taishun Mibu. He held a lecturer post at Taisho University, attested in 1985.

Ryoshu Koda focuses on Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Otani University, where he held a post from around 1929 to 1969, before serving as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from circa 1969 to 1978.

Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1941 to 1944 and later held an appointment there as professor emeritus, attested from 1988 to 2000.

Ryoshun Okubo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at Waseda University from around 1974 to 1983. He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University around 2004 and directed Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and was a graduate student researcher at Toyo University in 2015. He was also a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center that same year.
Ryotai Hatani (1883–1974) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Kyoto University from 1929 to 1943 and later served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University from around 1954 to 1974.

Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard Business School and trained under Kōun Yamada. He worked in banking and corporate posts, and became the head (Leiter) of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held appointments at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His appointments include Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuhiko Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1953 to 1955. He spent his career at Rissho University as lecturer, associate professor, professor (circa 1975–2002), and university president (circa 1992–1995).

Ryuichi Abe specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia, he served as Kao Associate Professor at Columbia (1998–2004) before becoming Edwin O. Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard around 2005.
Ryukai Mano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1991).
Ryuken Sato (1931–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the supervision of Tom Tillemans.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and served as professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1970 to 2003.

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Kyushu University and president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).
